overview: 26 official Qs (2008, 2012, 2017, 2024, 2025); Prelims 2024 alone has 9. Mauryas (Ashokan edicts, Arthashastra officers) and Indus sites are the core; Guptas, Vedic texts, Jainism and Harsha follow. Formats: one-liners on 'who/where/which inscription', NOT-questions (which is not a Harappan site / not by Harsha) and one 2025 matching.

possibility.what_they_ask: Meaning of a site name, site with an unusual feature (radial plan at Banawali), economic base, which listed site is NOT Harappan
Which Veda is musical (Sama), inscription naming Vedic gods outside India (Boghazkoi)
Parts of a stupa (anda, harmika, chhatri), Ashtanga Marga
Community that followed Jainism (merchants), patron king (Kharavela), Triratna matching

possibility.angle: Post-Mauryan dynasties and Alexander (leaf P1.1.3 general)
possibility.what_they_ask: Kushan ruler name, Alexander's invasion year, successors of Mauryas (Sungas)
Site of a major rock edict, Andhra site of a specific edict (Erragudi), Arthashastra officer for a function (Pautavadhyaksha)
Occasion of prisoner release (coronation anniversary), Rummindei tax reduction
Natural targets (APPSC asks inscriptions and sites): Sarnath lion capital, Barabar caves for Ajivikas, polished Chunar sandstone pillars, Arthashastra and Indica authors
Which king took the title Vikramaditya
Foreign traveller and the king of his visit, cause of post-Gupta trade decline
Author/subject of a Siddhanta, Varahamihira and Aryabhata works
Which book was NOT written by Harsha; natural targets: Hiuen Tsang, Kanauj and Prayag assemblies, Bana's Harshacharita

traps.trap: Pillar edict site offered for a rock edict [rock vs pillar]
traps.spot: Edict-type question with Allahabad/Delhi/Barabar among options
traps.fix: Major rock edicts: Girnar, Kalsi, Dhauli, Jaugada, Erragudi…; Allahabad, Delhi = pillars; Barabar = caves

traps.trap: Traveller paired with the wrong king
traps.spot: Chinese/Greek visitor with a list of rulers
traps.fix: Megasthenes – Chandragupta Maurya; Fa-Hien – Chandragupta II; Hiuen Tsang – Harsha

traps.trap: Court writer's work credited to the king
traps.spot: 'Not written by Harsha' with famous Sanskrit titles
traps.fix: Harsha: Ratnavali, Priyadarshika, Nagananda; Kadambari and Harshacharita are Bana's

traps.trap: Later-period site slipped into a Harappan list
traps.spot: NOT-question listing sites with similar-sounding names
traps.fix: Sohgaura = Mauryan copper plate; Sutkagendor, Surkotada, Rakhigarhi are Harappan
Pautava = weights and measures; Sulka = tolls; Panya = trade; Samstha = markets

traps.spot: Triratna/eightfold items in a religion matching
traps.fix: Ashtanga Marga = Buddhism; Triratna here = Jain (right faith, knowledge, conduct); Linga = Saivism; nature worship = animism

traps.trap: Neighbouring dynasty in the succession chain
traps.fix: Magadha: Maurya → Sunga (Pushyamitra, c. 185 BC) → Kanva

traps.trap: Year of a later event offered for Alexander

techniques.name: Edict-content map [edict → message]
techniques.how: Memorise each Ashokan inscription by its message: RE XIII Kalinga, PE V prisoner release, Rummindei tax cut, Erragudi minor edict on teachers. Match the stem's content to the site.
techniques.example: Lumbini revenue reduced to one-eighth → Rummindei; Maski only gives the name 'Asoka' [prelims-2024#2]

techniques.name: Name-meaning decode
techniques.how: Use the literal meaning of names and terms: Mohenjo-daro = mound of the dead; Sama = melody; Pautava = weights.

techniques.name: Odd-period elimination
techniques.how: In 'not Harappan' or 'not by X' questions, date every option; the one from another period or author is the answer.
techniques.example: Sutkagendor, Surkotada, Rakhigarhi Bronze Age; Sohgaura Mauryan → Sohgaura [prelims-2024#17]

techniques.name: Anchor-pair matching
techniques.how: Fix the surest pair (Linga–Saivism), strike codes without it, then check one more.
techniques.example: c-iv (Linga) appears only in option 3 → a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i [mains-2025-paper1#53]

techniques.name: Doctrine → social base reasoning
techniques.how: Infer followers from rules: strict ahimsa barred ploughing, so Jainism drew traders.

confusions.remember: Chandragupta Maurya vs Chandragupta II / Harsha
Girnar, Kalsi, Dhauli, Jaugada, Erragudi vs Allahabad, Delhi-Topra, Lauriya, Rampurva
Both Kurnool; Erragudi has major + minor edicts incl. teachers–Dhamma line
Lumbini tax reduction vs inscription naming 'Asoka'
Ratnavali, Priyadarshika, Nagananda vs Harshacharita, Kadambari
Vedic gods in Anatolia (c. 1380 BC) vs Rudradaman's Sanskrit inscription
Founder of Kushan rule vs most famous Kushan (78 CE, Saka era)
Radial streets vs three-part city with water reservoirs
Dome with anda-harmika-chhatri vs prayer hall / monastery

anchors: Mohenjo-daro = 'Mound of the Dead', excavated by R.D. Banerji 1922
Alexander enters India 327 BC; Hydaspes 326 BC
Pushyamitra Sunga ends Mauryas c. 185 BC
Ashoka's prisoner releases on coronation anniversaries (PE V)
Erragudi (Kurnool): Ashokan edict on teachers and Dhamma
Fa-Hien c. 399-411 CE under Chandragupta II
Boghazkoi c. 1380 BC: Indra, Varuna, Mitra, Nasatyas
checklist: Rock edict, pillar edict or cave? Major or minor?
Which king was ruling when the traveller came?
Is the work by the king or his court poet?
Date every option in 'not Harappan / not by X' questions
Decode the name or term literally
In matching, start from the least confusable pair
